tonight.headline: You are starting no defence
body: Week 3 has not started. Nothing on this roster kicks off before Sunday 11:00 Mexico City, so every row below is still changeable — and one of them has to change.

At 08:37 this morning you added Rashod Bateman and the paired drop was the Vikings D/ST, not Jonah Coleman. Your D/ST slot is now empty. An empty starting slot scores zero, and zero against a projected seven is the largest single point swing available to you this week. Fix that before anything else.

case.label: What the file says
case.body: Your fourteen players fill slots QB, RB, RB, FLEX, WR, WR, TE, K and six bench seats. Slot 16 — D/ST — is unoccupied. Every other team in Chem has one; the team-by-position print shows a DST line for all nine of them and none for AVIATO.

case.label: What it costs
case.body: Chem pays a defence 3 points a sack and tiers points-allowed at 10 / 7 / 4 / 1. A streamed defence against a bad offence is a 7-to-12 point slot here, not a 5-point one. You are currently conceding all of it.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: ESPN's roster endpoint is mis-reporting an occupied slot as empty. The activity log records the Vikings D/ST leaving AVIATO at 09-23T14:37Z and the Vikings D/ST now sits on the Chem wire as a free agent, so two independent parts of the same file agree. If you can see a defence in your ESPN lineup, ignore this entire brief's first card and tell the next run.

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Cincinnati kick off Sunday 11:00 Mexico City
doFirst.title: Add the Bengals D/ST, drop Jonah Coleman
doFirst.subtitle: Cincinnati are a free agent here, so this costs no waiver priority — only the roster seat. It turns a guaranteed zero into the best defensive draw on the board.

case.label: The hole
case.body: You have no defence at all. This is not an upgrade card, it is a slot that scores zero until something is in it.

case.label: Why Cincinnati
case.body: FantasyPros rank them DST4 this week at 6% rostered nationally and call them the number one scoring defence in fantasy so far this season. They travel to Pittsburgh, who scored three points against New England, took four sacks and rank dead last in the league in yards per play. Cincinnati have recorded four sacks in each of their first two games and finished with double-digit fantasy points both weeks.

case.label: Why it is worth more in Chem than the number says
case.body: Chem's D/ST scoring is not IPADE's. Sacks pay 3 here and the points-allowed tiers are 10 / 7 / 4 / 1 — Chem pays 7 for holding an opponent under seven points and 10 for a shutout, where IPADE pays 4 and 5. A defence facing the league's worst offence is worth materially more in this league than its ESPN projection of 6.9 suggests.

case.label: The conflict, stated
case.body: Jaylen Warren is your starting running back and he plays for Pittsburgh, so you would be starting a defence against your own back. In full PPR that conflict is weaker than it looks: Warren's value here is receptions, and a Pittsburgh deficit puts him on the field for passing downs. Cincinnati holding Pittsburgh to seven does not zero Warren; it changes which kind of touches he gets.

case.label: Why the drop is Coleman and not Bateman
case.body: This morning's card named Jonah Coleman as the drop and nothing has happened since to change that — following the standing plan is not churn, reversing it is. Coleman has a sprained ankle of his own from the Jacksonville game and ESPN prices that at 1.7. Dropping Bateman instead would reverse an add made eight hours ago, which the decision log records as failing twice on this roster.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Cincinnati are ruled out of the sack business by Friday's report — Trey Hendrickson or a starting corner appearing as out — or Pittsburgh name a quarterback change that raises their floor. It also closes wrong if Coleman is cleared and Denver rule both J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey out on Friday, which is the branch the second card covers.

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Fallback only — decide on Friday's Denver report
doFirst.title: Same defence, different drop: Bateman instead of Coleman
doFirst.subtitle: Unarmed. Fire this one only if Friday's Denver report clears Coleman's ankle and rules out both Dobbins and Harvey.

case.label: The branch
case.body: FantasyPros' Week 3 waiver column has Jonah Coleman taking over lead back duties in Denver — ten carries, 39 yards and a touchdown in Week 2 — after J.K. Dobbins left with a hamstring and RJ Harvey was already out. If that is the Friday picture and Coleman is cleared, he is a starting running back and not a drop.

case.label: Where ESPN and reporting disagree
case.body: ESPN projects Coleman 1.7. The reporting describes a lead back. Both can be true: the 1.7 is pricing his own sprained ankle, not his role. Believe the projection while the ankle is unresolved and the reporting the moment it clears — that is the whole content of this card.

case.label: Why Bateman becomes the drop
case.body: Bateman's case was a 93% snap share in a Week 2 played without Zay Flowers. Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said on 21 September that Flowers has a 'good shot' to play against Dallas. The condition that made Bateman worth a roster seat is the condition that is closing.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Denver listing Dobbins as a full participant, or Coleman missing Wednesday and Thursday practice. Either makes Coleman the drop again and this card never fires.

whatWentWrong.title: The unarmed card was fired, and your defence paid for it
whatWentWrong.lead: This morning's only card was a ghost — 'Fallback only, do not fire today'. It fired at 08:37 Mexico City, and the drop attached to it was the Vikings D/ST rather than Jonah Coleman.

case.label: The sequence
case.body: 09-23T14:37Z: AVIATO ADD Rashod Bateman. 09-23T14:37Z: AVIATO DROP Vikings D/ST. Those are the two most recent AVIATO entries in the activity log. The Vikings had been added that same morning — this morning's brief lists 'Claim the Vikings D/ST, drop the Ravens' among the calls it got right.

case.label: What it cost
case.body: The Vikings went from acquired to discarded inside seven hours, and the seat they were filling is mandatory. Chem starts one D/ST and there is no way to field a legal lineup without one.

case.label: The honest part
case.body: The card's subtitle named Jonah Coleman as the drop and the action payload carried dropPlayerId 4702555, which is Coleman. The brief was specific. The execution was not, and a brief cannot be specific enough to survive a different player being selected in the app.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: If it turns out ESPN applied a different drop than the one selected — a roster-limit auto-drop, say — then this is a platform behaviour to design around rather than an execution slip, and the next run should stop naming drops inside add cards and publish them as two separate actions.

whatWentWrong.title: Zay Flowers is expected to play, which was the condition that should have stopped the add
whatWentWrong.lead: Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said on 21 September that Flowers has a 'good shot' to play in Week 3 against Dallas. Bateman's entire case was the game Flowers missed.

case.label: The thesis as written
case.body: The morning card read: 'Week 2 without Zay Flowers: 93% of Baltimore's snaps with no other Ravens receiver above 55%, team lead in targets, catches and yards.' Every clause in that sentence depends on Flowers being absent.

case.label: The reporting
case.body: Flowers is dealing with a hamstring. NBC Sports carried Minter's 'good shot' line on 21 September. He has not been ruled out at any point this week and Baltimore have not published a Friday designation yet.

case.label: Why it still connects to today's card
case.body: It is the reason the second Do-first card exists. If Flowers plays, Bateman is a WR3 on a roster that has no room for one, and he becomes the drop the moment Coleman's ankle resolves the other way.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Baltimore rule Flowers out on Friday. Bateman then reverts to the 93%-snap-share receiver the morning card described and the add was simply early rather than wrong.

whatWentWrong.title: Eddy Pineiro is the 17th-best kicker this week and he is staying anyway
whatWentWrong.lead: Pro Football Network rank Pineiro K17 for Week 3. Evan McPherson is K1 and a free agent in this league. You are not going to get him.

case.label: The comparison, run as required
case.body: PFN's Week 3 board: McPherson K1 (Cincinnati at Pittsburgh, 37.3% owned here and a free agent), Trey Smack K4 (24.5%, free agent), Jason Myers K5, Will Reichard K9, Chase McLaughlin K10, Tyler Bass K12, Eddy Pineiro K17. The gap between K1 and K17 is real, not noise.

case.label: Why the answer is still hold
case.body: You have fourteen players and fourteen roster spots, so every add is a drop. The one drop you have is spoken for by a mandatory empty starting slot worth roughly seven points against a certain zero. The kicker gap is worth perhaps two. You cannot spend the same seat twice.

case.label: The churn point
case.body: Pineiro arrived this morning — the 13:05Z brief lists 'Claim Eddy Pineiro, drop Tyler Loop' among its correct calls. Moving him tonight would be the second change to the kicker seat in one day, which is the exact pattern the strategy document was written to stop.

case.label: When to act
case.body: 30 September, when the seven-day churn window on the kicker seat expires, and the answer then is whoever tops that week's board among free agents. If Pineiro finishes outside the top twenty in Week 3 while McPherson finishes top five, the seat reopens on schedule rather than early.

worthALook.name: Panthers D/ST
worthALook.lead: The alternative defence, and the reason it is not the card.

case.label: The case for them
case.body: FantasyPros rank Carolina DST2 this week. They forced five turnovers against Atlanta in Week 2 and they draw Deshaun Watson, who FantasyLife note puts the ball at risk regularly and has taken seven sacks in two games. Their ownership moved +28.32 in a day, the largest single defensive move on the Chem wire.

case.label: The number that gives me pause
case.body: Panthers.com's Wednesday practice report has outside linebacker Jaelan Phillips and linebacker Devin Lloyd not practising. Carolina's Week 2 was a pass rush and a turnover game; that is the part of it that is questionable this week, and the Bengals' four-sacks-a-game rate has no such asterisk.

case.label: The other collision
case.body: Denzel Boston is on your bench and plays for Cleveland. Taking Carolina's defence means rooting against a receiver you might otherwise promote.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Phillips and Lloyd both practising in full on Friday, which restores the pass rush the ranking is built on. At that point Carolina are the better of the two and the card's add should be -16029 instead of -16004.

worthALook.name: Tre Tucker
worthALook.lead: Carried forward unchanged from this morning, and still a watch row rather than a card.

case.label: Why he is still here
case.body: Five catches, 119 yards and a touchdown on seven targets at the Chargers in Week 2, and a free agent here so he costs no priority. His ownership moved +11.66 in a day.

case.label: Why he is not a card
case.body: Every roster seat you have is committed. The one drop available this week goes to a mandatory empty defensive slot, and a fourth receiver does not outrank that.

case.label: The honest weakness
case.body: Brock Bowers is expected back — Schefter said he would be surprised if Bowers were not on the field this week. Tucker's Week 2 came with Bowers out, which is the same shape of case as Bateman's and deserves the same scepticism.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Bowers returning and Tucker still clearing seven targets, which would say the role is his rather than the absence's. Or the Denver report clearing Coleman, which frees the seat the first card is using.

doNotChase.name: Kyle Pitts Sr.
doNotChase.lead: You dropped him yesterday, the quarterback risk that justified it has gone away, and he is still not the answer.

case.label: What changed in his favour
case.body: Atlanta named Michael Penix Jr. the Week 3 starter against Green Bay on Monday — NFL.com and FOX both carried it. Cooper Rush threw a league-high four interceptions in two starts and was benched at half-time against Carolina; Jack Strand, the undrafted rookie who replaced him, fared no better. The third-string-quarterback risk that this system exists to catch is genuinely closed for Pitts.

case.label: Why he is still wrong for this roster
case.body: Chem's flex is RB/WR only. A second tight end cannot enter your lineup in any week, whatever he scores. This is structural and no amount of Penix fixes it.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: His ownership fell 3.42 today, so the market is not fighting you for him either.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Isaiah Likely appearing on a Giants injury report. That is the only condition that makes a second startable tight end necessary rather than unusable, and it is the same clause carried from yesterday.

doNotChase.sources: NFL.com · FOX Sports · ESPN league file

doNotChase.name: Dalton Schultz
doNotChase.lead: The biggest single ownership move on either wire today, and a decline for the same structural reason.

case.label: Why the market is moving
case.body: Plus 29.82 rostered in a day. Dallas Goedert is doubtful and Schultz is the named beneficiary at tight end in Houston; the number is the market catching up to that, and the market is right about him.

case.label: The number that kills it here
case.body: Zero. That is how many points a second tight end can score in a Chem lineup, because slot 3 takes RB and WR only. The correct reaction to a tight end rising 29.82 in this league is to notice and do nothing.

case.label: Where this belongs instead
case.body: IPADE, whose flex is slot 23 and takes a tight end. That is the league where a second startable tight end has value, and it is covered in that brief.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Isaiah Likely being ruled out. Same condition as the Pitts row, and if it fires, one of the two is the answer rather than both.

doNotChase.name: Jaxson Dart
doNotChase.lead: Still the largest ownership anomaly on this wire, and the reporting got worse rather than better.

case.label: What the number says
case.body: A quarterback rostered in the low eighties nationally, sitting free in a ten-team league. On the wire bands that is the strongest signal there is.

case.label: What the reporting says
case.body: Giants.com now has it as Dart missing the rest of the regular season with the MCL sprain, with Jameis Winston named the starter. The anomaly is not an opportunity; it is nine other managers having read the same news.

case.label: And the structural point
case.body: Chem starts one quarterback and yours is Josh Allen at 23.8. There is no version of this where Dart enters your lineup.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: The Giants publishing a dated return. Nothing short of that, and even then Allen starts.

settled.title: Publish the Bateman add as a ghost card and expect it to stay unarmed (23 September, 13:05Z)
settled.result: It fired within ninety minutes and took the Vikings D/ST with it. The ghost mechanism did not do the job it was designed for; treat a ghost card as a recommendation that may be acted on, not as one that will not be.

settled.title: Hold Isaiah Likely through the Giants quarterback change (22 September)
settled.result: Dart is now out for the regular season and Winston is the settled starter. SI rank Likely TE9 for Week 3. Holding through the noise was right.

settled.title: Decline Kyle Pitts on structure rather than on the quarterback (23 September)
settled.result: Penix was named the Week 3 starter on Monday, so the quarterback objection evaporated — and the structural objection, that Chem's flex takes no tight end, did not. The decline survived the reason changing under it, which is the point of writing the structural one down.

settled.title: Hold Jaylen Warren through the Dowdle threat (13 September, reviewed weekly)
settled.result: Dowdle exited Week 2 with a toe injury and was ruled out. The falsification clause was Dowdle out-touching him two weeks running; that branch is further from firing than it was.

settled.title: Hold the Vikings D/ST and Eddy Pineiro as a settled pair (23 September, 07:05Z)
settled.result: Half of it was undone by 08:37 the same morning. The defence half of that thesis is dead — not because the analysis was wrong, but because the unit was dropped. Recorded so the next run does not carry a hold on a player who is no longer on the roster.

cannotSee.label: Every matchup tile on this roster is dashed
cannotSee.body: No defence-versus-position table could be retrieved this run. FantasyPros' points-allowed page and ESPN's matchup-rankings column both render their tables in JavaScript and return only navigation to a fetch. Fourteen dashed tiles mean fourteen defences I did not check, not fourteen average draws. The two graded rows in the IPADE brief came from prose in start/sit columns, which is the only route that worked.

cannotSee.label: Friday designations do not exist yet
cannotSee.body: It is Wednesday afternoon. Zay Flowers, Jaylen Warren, Jalen Coker, Kyle Monangai and Jonah Coleman are all carrying designations that will be resolved by a Friday report this brief cannot see. Both Do-first cards are built to branch on that report rather than to pre-empt it.

cannotSee.label: Rival claims are invisible
cannotSee.body: ESPN returns only your own pending claims. Waivers in Chem clear at 01:00 Mexico City tonight, and whether another manager has a claim in on the Bengals, the Panthers or anyone else is not in this file. Chem's priority resets weekly so a lost claim costs nothing lasting — but the Bengals are a free agent, which means first come rather than priority order, and that is a reason to act tonight rather than Saturday.

cannotSee.label: Whether the empty slot is recoverable at no cost
cannotSee.body: The Vikings D/ST left your roster at 14:37Z and shows on the wire with status FREEAGENT, which is unusual for a same-day drop and suggests Chem does not send defences to waivers. If that reading is wrong and they are actually on a waiver period the file is not showing, the Bengals are unaffected — they were a free agent before today.

cannotSee.label: seasonProj is live but it does not price availability
cannotSee.body: The season projections move between snapshots, so the runbook's worry that they are a preseason artifact is not what is happening. What they do not do is price a player being unavailable: Jonah Coleman carries a full-season number while nursing an ankle. Use them to narrow a list, never to settle one.

cannotSee.label: No trade is proposed in Chem this week
cannotSee.body: Standing policy treats weeks 1 to 3 as noise and reacts to role news rather than box scores. Nothing in this snapshot is a role change big enough to price a trade against, and your roster's problem this week is a missing defence rather than a missing starter. The first real trade window is weeks 4 to 6.
